title: Build an AI/ML Research Project: 7 Rules
description: Seven rules for turning an AI/ML idea into a focused, fair, reproducible and evidence-led research project.
cta_text: Read the Complete AI/ML Research Guide

pages.heading: Starting AI/ML Research? Follow These 7 Rules
pages.text: Strong research connects one measurable problem to suitable data, a fair baseline, controlled experiments and honest analysis.
pages.alt: Engineering student beginning an AI research project beside an edge camera prototype

pages.heading: 1. Start With the Problem
pages.text: Name the application, user, unresolved limitation and measurable outcome before choosing an algorithm. A field like computer vision is not yet a research question.
pages.alt: Engineering student narrowing a broad AI topic into one measurable research problem

pages.heading: 2. Prove the Gap With Literature
pages.text: Compare recent papers by data, method, baseline, metrics, findings and limits. Treat repeated weaknesses as leads—not automatic proof of novelty.
pages.alt: AI researcher comparing papers in a structured literature review matrix

pages.heading: 3. Audit the Dataset First
pages.text: Check size, balance, duplicates, labels, representativeness, licensing and leakage risk. A complex model cannot rescue unsuitable evidence.
pages.alt: Student auditing the balance and quality of an image dataset for an AI experiment

pages.heading: 4. Establish a Fair Baseline
pages.text: Start with a simple relevant method, then compare stronger approaches under the same data split, preprocessing and evaluation conditions.
pages.alt: Engineering student comparing baseline and advanced AI model performance

pages.heading: 5. Keep the Test Set Sealed
pages.text: Split before learned preprocessing. Use training data to fit, validation data to choose, and the test set only for the final unbiased evaluation.
pages.alt: Student separating machine learning data into three distinct protected groups

pages.heading: 6. Measure the Error That Matters
pages.text: Accuracy alone may hide minority-class failures. Choose precision, recall, F1, AUC, latency or cost according to the real decision and constraint.
pages.alt: AI researcher examining a confusion matrix and multiple model evaluation measures

pages.heading: 7. Make Every Result Reproducible
pages.text: Record dataset version, splits, preprocessing, code, seeds, hyperparameters, library versions and hardware. Then analyze failures and limitations.
pages.alt: Student documenting reproducible AI experiments beside a tested edge device

pages.heading: Research Is a Chain of Evidence
pages.text: Problem to gap. Gap to experiment. Experiment to result. Result to defensible contribution. Keep every link visible and testable.
pages.alt: Prepared engineering student reviewing a complete evidence-led AI research project
